subject: Cascade Medical: urgent - VPC throughput suppression & proposed tuning
messages:

Subject: Unexplained throughput collapse - private VPC

Olga,

We started seeing our private deployment drop from ~1200 requests/minute to sub-200 during the overnight run at ~01:00 PT. Latency jumped to 950ms p95 and we saw a sudden increase in 504s. This is the pipeline that runs patient-note generation for clinic shift handoffs so it's urgent.

Attached are the logs around 00:45-01:15 and the kernel snapshots requested by your team last month (svc_logs_20260818.tgz). We're happy to hop on a call.

Aaron
Dr. Aaron Feldman
Director of Data Systems | Cascade Medical

On Tue, 18 Aug 2026 at 09:34, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether the deployment was on the 2.2.1 runtime image or the 2.3-rc build? Also, did you apply the kernel changes we advised last month?

Quick initial findings after a 10-min look at the tarball and metrics you sent:
- There is a clear KV cache eviction wave starting at 00:49 that coincides with a burst of long-context requests (avg seq len +45%)
- We also see an uptick in token fan-out retries from the batching layer which doubles worker load briefly
- The node CPU shows a recurring 15s pause (symmetric across GPUs) consistent with a driver-level stall — need kernel diff to validate (please share kernel-cfg-diff.txt)

Immediate recommended mitigations (non-disruptive):
1) Turn on per-route short-circuit cache (prefix-only) to avoid large-context cache thrash
2) Reduce max-batch-size by 20% for the next 60 minutes to lower queue head-of-line blocking
3) Enable fallback routing to the 7B quantized variant for low-priority patient-note endpoints

I'll prepare a short playbook and a canary tweak we can roll in the next 30–45 minutes. If we see sustained >20% error rate, escalate to execs.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment requested: kernel-cfg-diff.txt

Thanks Rishi — attaching the kernel diff we ran last month. We are on the 2.2.1 runtime image (we didn't move to 2.3-rc).

The infra team also confirmed we had a large batch of long-context exports queued from 23:50-00:05 that night (we had a billing-backfill job). We can pause that job if the mitigation requires it.

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Unexplained throughput collapse - private VPC

Maya — thank you.
We're going to implement Rishi's mitigations in a staged fashion:
- 11:15: reduce max-batch-size by 20% on the VPC pool (no restart)
- 11:25: enable prefix-only KV caching for patient-note route (will be reversible)
- 11:40: enable fallback routing (7B-quantized) for non-interactive endpoints and monitor errors

Diego will watch the GPU driver logs and coordinate with your infra for kernel-level checks. Monica (CS) here — if everything looks stable after 60 minutes we'll schedule a 1-hour post-mortem this afternoon to capture root cause and add hard SLOs to prevent recurrence.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained throughput collapse - private VPC

Update from the field: after the batch-size reduction and prefix-only caching we saw p95 drop from 950ms to ~210ms and throughput recovering to ~950 requests/min within 18 minutes. The kernel diff shows a subtle scheduling back-off introduced by a vendor patch — when combined with the eviction wave it amplified tail latency.

I'll upload a small csv with eviction counts; logging indicates KV-cache churn spiking at 00:49 and again at 01:03. We'll follow up with an ops playbook:
- Block the overnight billing backfill until we apply a versioned throttle
- Apply a small kernel revert on a canary host (requires your infra approval)
- Add a short-term auto-fallback policy to route >1200 token requests to a dedicated lane to avoid cache poisoning

Diego
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: kvcache-eviction-metrics.csv (2.2MB)
